newsitem.title: UK: Lanica's Galileo confirms was to bid for UK's CWS.
newsitem.headline: Lanica's Galileo confirms was to bid for UK's CWS.

text.p: Galileo Group Ltd confirmed on Friday it had been stopped from making an intended offer for Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) by legal action.

Galileo, an offshoot of Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica, said in a statement it had intended to make formal proposals for the conversion of the mutually-owned supermarkets to funeral parlour mammoth to a limited company which it would then offer to buy.

There was intense speculation on Friday that entrepreneur Andrew Regan, who heads Lanica, was about to make a 1.0-1.5 billion pound ($2.4 billion) bid for the 153-year-old CWS, which was formed by a group called the "Rochdale Pioneers" in Lancashire, north west England, in 1844.

Little is known of Galileo but British newspapers have reported that it is partly owned by Lanica, with backing from City institutions such as Schroders, Jupiter Asset Management and stockbroker Killick & Co.

Previously, Regan's ambition was believed to be in buying the Co-op's non-food businesses, which include the profitable Co-operative Bank, the Co-operative Insurance Society (CIS), farms, factories and travel agents.
The CWS, which earlier this week reported a fall in pre-tax profits for 1996, has repeatedly rejected any suggestion of selling any of its businesses to Regan. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
